bihar_raw_news.title: "No compromise on safety, public convenience": Bihar CM sets 2028 deadline for Patna ...
bihar_raw_news.content: "No compromise on safety, public convenience": Bihar CM sets 2028 deadline for Patna Metro completion ANI | Updated: Oct 11, 2026 16:12 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], October 11 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday inspected the ongoing construction work of the Patna Metro Rail project along Nehru Path and directed officials to ensure that the entire project is completed by the year 2028. During the on-site inspection, the Chief Minister visited key stretches, including the Income Tax roundabout, High Court roundabout, and the area near the Hanuman temple, taking stock of the progress from senior project officials. Emphasizing commuter convenience, the Chief Minister directed the authorities to construct two foot overbridges (FOBs) on Nehru Path—one near JD Women’s College and another near the High Court roundabout–Bihar Museum junction. The Chief Minister stressed that execution must strictly adhere to prescribed quality and safety norms while ensuring minimal disruption to the daily lives of citizens. "Work must be executed in an organized and coordinated manner so that citizens face minimum inconvenience. Traffic management around construction sites, smooth pedestrian and vehicular movement, and public safety must be given top priority," the Chief Minister instructed officials, adding that urban development should go hand-in-hand with civic ease. Terming the metro project crucial for the capital city's public transport network, Choudhary called for regular monitoring and seamless coordination among all executing agencies. He made it clear that while speeding up construction is essential, there must be no compromise on quality, safety standards, or civic amenities. The inspection was attended by Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary, Cooperative Minister Ram Kripal Yadav, and Science, Technology & Technical Education Minister Sheela Kumari. Senior administrative officials present on the occasion included Principal Secretary (Urban Development & Housing and Finance) Vinay Kumar, Secretary (Road Construction) Pankaj Kumar Pal, Secretary to the CM Lokesh Kumar Singh, Patna Metro Rail Project Managing Director Sandeep Kumar R. Pudakalkatti, Building Construction Secretary Pranav Kumar, Urban Development Secretary Animesh Kumar Parashar, Patna District Magistrate Kundan Kumar, and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Kartikeya K. Sharma. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM seeks two BHU centres, ₹5275 crore for new government colleges - ET Education
bihar_raw_news.content: Higher Education 2 min read Bihar CM seeks two BHU centres, ₹5,275 crore for new government colleges Samrat Choudhary urges Centre to fund infrastructure in 211 degree colleges, expedite Vikramshila University’s revival and open more Kendriya Vidyalayas in the state. Madan Kumar & madan.kumar TOI.in Published On Oct 11, 2026 at 12:00 PM IST Select ETEducation as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook CM urges Ce ntre to open two units of BHU in Bihar Patna: CM Samrat Choudhary on Saturday urged the Centre to establish at least two Banaras Hindu University (BHU) centres in Bihar, saying the move would expand higher education opportunities for students and strengthen academic activity in the state. He made the request to Union education minister Pralhad Joshi during a review meeting at Samvad Hall in the chief minister’s secretariat in Patna, where issues concerning the quality of higher and school education and infrastructure in educational institutions were discussed. The meeting was jointly chaired by Samrat and Joshi. Advt Samrat sought Rs 5,275 crore from the Centre for infrastructure development in 211 newly opened govt degree colleges in Bihar, calculated at Rs 25 crore per college. He said the funds were needed to provide essential facilities at these institutions. The CM also pressed for action on the re-establishment of Vikramshila University near Bhagalpur, noting that 220 acres of land had been transferred to the university on July 15 this year. He urged the Union govt to take the next steps at the earliest. Samrat also requested the opening of more Kendriya Vidyalayas in Bihar. He said additional central schools would give students better access to quality education and help expand educational facilities across the state. Reviewing education projects, Samrat and Joshi emphasised time-bound implementation and improved access to educational facilities. Officials from the Centre and state govts made presentations on schemes and their implementation. Anand Rao B Patil, additional secretary, higher education, govt of India; Archana Sharma Awasthi, additional secretary, department of school education and literacy, govt of India; and Amarjeet Duggal of the same department briefed the meeting on centrally sponsored schemes. Rajiv Roushan, secretary, education and higher education department, govt of Bihar, presented details of scheme implementation and state govt initiatives. Advt Earlier in the day, Samrat and Joshi inaugurated the state-level prize distribution ceremony for Seva Chitra and speech competitions, organised by the education department at Bapu Sabhagar in Patna. Held under the Seva Hi Sankalp campaign, the competitions drew participation from students of 95,195 govt and private schools across 38 districts. Samrat congratulated the students and extended his good wishes to them. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's Game-Changing Reforms: Streamlining Business and Attracting Investment, ETGovernment
bihar_raw_news.content: Governance 5 min read From red tape to right to business: Bihar unveils major reforms to attract investments, accelerate industrialisation Bihar’s new Ease of Doing Business framework promises faster approvals, self-certification and fewer inspections, aiming to attract investment, accelerate industrialisation and generate employment. Anoop Verma ETGovernment Published On Oct 11, 2026 at 07:37 AM IST Select ETGovernment as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary Bihar’s Ease of Doing Business Act, 2026, introduces a major shift in industrial governance, allowing enterprises to begin operations through self-declaration, securing time-bound approvals and establishing a single authority responsible for investment clearances. The reforms could strengthen Bihar’s competitiveness as an industrial destination, provided implementation matches legislative ambition. The state is attempting to dismantle one of the most persistent barriers to industrialisation in India: the complex regulatory system that forces entrepreneurs to navigate multiple departments, secure numerous permissions and endure uncertain approval timelines before establishing a business. Advt Through three notifications issued on October 9, 2026, under the Bihar Ease of Doing Business Act, 2026, the state government has initiated a potentially significant transformation in its industrial governance framework. The legislation seeks to replace permission-based administration with a system founded on entrepreneurial freedom, regulatory accountability, self-certification and time-bound decision-making. For a state seeking to accelerate manufacturing, attract private investment and generate employment, the reforms represent an important institutional intervention. The Department of Industries issued Gazette Notifications 1270, 1271 and 1272, operationalising different provisions of the legislation, which was originally published on September 16, 2026, as Bihar Act 32 of 2026. Notification 1271 establishes the framework for what the government describes as the Right to Business , while Notification 1272 designates a single nodal agency for investment-related approvals. Notification 1270 concerns the implementation of Section 27 read with Schedule VII, according to the official Gazette index. Its detailed provisions could not be independently verified from the available text. Together, the notifications indicate Bihar's intention to shift the relationship between entrepreneurs and regulatory authorities from administrative discretion towards predictable, rules-based governance. From regulatory permissions to entrepreneurial freedom The most consequential provision concerns the right of enterprises to commence operations through self-declaration. Under Sections 19 and 20 of the Act, entrepreneurs intending to establish or expand businesses can submit a Declaration of Intent through the state's Single Window System. Advt The District Empowered Committee will subsequently issue a Certificate of In-Principle Approval (CIPA). The certificate remains valid for three years, enabling enterprises to establish, construct and operate while obtaining applicable regular approvals within the stipulated period. The legislation prescribes approval timelines of five working days for micro enterprises, ten working days for small enterprises and fifteen working days for medium and large enterprises. Where authorities fail to act within these periods, approval is deemed to have been granted. Equally significant is the restriction on routine inspections. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said the world is looking for solutions to emerging challenges and expressed confidence that India’s youth have the talent and potential to provide them. Mr Modi was speaking at Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya in Chennai this evening. Mr Modi stressed that the youth will play a crucial role in realising the vision of a Viksit Bharat, or a developed India. He said, ‘India offers immense opportunities for young people,’ and urged them to realise their potential and contribute to the nation’s development. He asserted that the innovative ideas and solutions developed by young people would shape not only India’s future but also the future of the world. The Prime Minister expressed confidence that the country’s aspirations could be achieved through collective efforts. Highlighting India’s manufacturing growth, Mr. Modi said, the expansion of the sector has generated direct and indirect employment opportunities for young people. He noted that India’s defence exports had increased 50-fold, while engineering exports had also reached a new record. The Prime Minister said India has become the world’s second-largest mobile phone manufacturer. He added that electronics exports have increased 11-fold since 2014. Mr. Modi also highlighted the expansion of Metro rail services, saying the number of cities with Metro connectivity had increased from five in 2014 to 25 at present. Referring to Tamil Nadu’s development, the Prime Minister said governments may change, but his commitment to the state’s progress and the welfare of its people remained steadfast. He said he will work with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to take the state’s development journey forward. On the occasion, Mr. Modi also congratulated Vishwa Hindu Vidya Kendra on completing 50 years. Recalling its beginnings in 1975 as a small school in Chennai’s West Mambalam area, he said the institution had started with just seven students, limited facilities and no permanent building. He credited its growth to determination and a strong spirit of service.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 372 PM Modi Launches Development Projects Worth ₹13,000 Crore in Tamil Nadu
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for a series of development projects worth more than 13,000 crore rupees across Tamil Nadu at an event held at IIT-Madras in Chennai today. The projects span road and rail transport, port infrastructure, petroleum and scientific research. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay was also present on the occasion. The projects include National Highway works worth around 3,700 crore rupees, initiatives at Chennai Port, Kamarajar Port and V. O. Chidambaranar Port, and the development of railway stations under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme. Addressing the gathering, Prime Minister Modi described the inauguration of projects worth 13-thousand crore rupees in Tamil Nadu as a historic occasion, saying the initiatives will improve connectivity, strengthen industry and trade, and create employment opportunities for the state’s youth. Mr. Modi said the projects will make daily travel easier and support the state’s economic growth. Recalling his interactions with former Tamil Nadu Chief Ministers M. Karunanidhi and J. Jayalalithaa, Mr. Modi said he had also worked with former Chief Ministers O. Panneerselvam, Edappadi K. Palaniswami and M. K. Stalin during his tenure as Prime Minister. He said that despite changes in governments, his commitment to the development of Tamil Nadu and the welfare of its people had remained unchanged. He added that he would continue this journey in cooperation with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. Recalling his journey in public service, Mr. Modi said he had completed 25 years as head of government, having taken the oath as Gujarat Chief Minister in October 2001 before becoming Prime Minister. Mr. Modi said India’s progress draws strength from its rich cultural heritage, scientific achievements and modern infrastructure. He cited Tamil Nadu’s temples, scientific institutions and Metro rail network as examples of how tradition and modern development can go hand in hand. The Prime Minister also extended Navaratri greetings to the people of the state. Mr. Modi also dedicated to the nation the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras. The centre is part of a pioneering scientific initiative to map more than 100 human brains and create three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution. The research will cover the entire human lifespan, from the foetal stage to old age. The Prime Minister also released C-STROKE, a unique atlas of the human brain affected by ischaemic stroke. Featuring more than 1,000 annotated microscopic sections, the atlas is expected to help researchers worldwide identify new targets for treatment. Earlier in the day, Mr. Modi inaugurated the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase Two of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around 4,900 crore rupees. The Prime Minister and Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay jointly flagged off the new Metro services and travelled on the train. The newly inaugurated stretch is part of Corridor Four of Phase Two. It includes 11 elevated Metro stations spread across approximately 15 kilometres. The projects are aimed at strengthening transport connectivity, improving infrastructure and advancing scientific research in Tamil Nadu.

national_raw_news.content: The Supreme Court today directed authorities to ensure that people gathering peacefully are not illegally detained and that the free movement of people is allowed, subject to traffic regulations. It also called for a review of barricading arrangements in Delhi and directed the Centre to ensure that metro services operate according to their normal schedule and that internet services remain uninterrupted, subject to law and order requirements. The court said metro and train services should function normally in accordance with the prevailing law and order situation. It further directed that lawyers must not be obstructed from discharging their professional duties. Issuing notice to the Centre on a plea seeking initiation of contempt proceedings against authorities over alleged violations of its directions, the Supreme Court said it would hear all parties and ensure that no inconvenience was caused. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta informed the court that entry and exit had been restricted at only 45 of the 303 stations across the metro network on October 10. The court’s directions came amid concerns over restrictions on movement and the functioning of public services in connection with protests in the national capital. The Supreme Court emphasised that peaceful assembly, the movement of people and the discharge of professional duties by lawyers should not be unnecessarily obstructed, while noting that these activities remained subject to applicable laws and traffic regulations. The court said it would hear all concerned parties before proceeding further on the contempt pleas.

national_raw_news.title: RBI Tightens Rupee Derivatives Rules, Cuts Dollar Transaction Limit to $5 Million 2 hours ago 34
national_raw_news.content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has introduced fresh restrictions on rupee derivatives to curb currency speculation and maintain an orderly foreign exchange market. The central bank has reduced the threshold for foreign exchange derivative transactions without underlying exposure from 100 million to 5 million dollars across authorised dealers and recognised stock exchanges. Under the new directions, authorised dealers will not be allowed to rebook rupee-involving foreign exchange derivative contracts cancelled after the issuance of the directions. However, rollover of contracts upon maturity will continue to be permitted. The RBI has also directed users hedging contracted exposures to confirm that the same underlying exposure has not been hedged with another authorised dealer. Additionally, the RBI has introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR), requiring authorised dealers to maintain a cash reserve equivalent to 20 per cent of the rupee value of qualifying derivative contracts exceeding $2 million that hedge current-account exposures involving the purchase of foreign currency against the rupee. The reserve must be maintained daily until the contract is terminated. The central bank has warned that attempts to circumvent the requirements through multiple transactions will be treated as violations. Authorised dealers must also report FERR details daily through the Centralised Information Management System. While the directions under Circular No. 25 take effect immediately, the FERR requirements under Circular No. 26 apply to contracts undertaken after the issuance of the directions. The measures aim to strengthen market discipline, improve risk management and ensure transparency in the foreign exchange market.

national_raw_news.title: Maharashtra CM Fadnavis Launches Second Phase of Mukhyamantri Samruddha Panchayat Raj Abhiyan 2.0 39 mins ago 16
national_raw_news.content: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis today launched the second phase of the Mukhyamantri Samruddha Panchayat Raj Abhiyan 2.0 in Nashik. Addressing the gathering, the Chief Minister called for collective efforts to achieve sustainable rural development, with a special focus on water conservation and drought prevention. He assured that the state government would provide the necessary funds for water conservation projects. Mr. Fadnavis stressed the need to desilt village ponds, repair check dams and promote rainwater harvesting. He said drinking water must be given top priority, along with ensuring adequate water for livestock and the upcoming rabi crop season. He also assured support for fodder availability and farmers affected by adverse weather conditions. Speaking at the event, Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Jaykumar Gore said the first phase saw the participation of 5,644 gram panchayats. It also witnessed the issuance of 69.13 lakh Ayushman cards and the completion of 2,706 kilometres of roads, besides progress in housing, sanitation and water-recharge projects. During the programme, the Chief Minister felicitated outstanding Zilla Parishads, Panchayat Samitis and Gram Panchayats for their performance in 2025-26. Nashik, Pune and Sangli topped the Zilla Parishad category, while Adachiwadi village in Pune district secured first place among Gram Panchayats. Several public representatives, senior officials and village heads from across Maharashtra attended the event.
